research_task.title: Project the viscous gap through Leray

summary: For one explicit smooth compact radial-vortex correction on R3, a compact divergence-free differentiated test gives a pressure-invariant Leray lower bound whose leading viscous term is proportional to nu times amplitude times the transverse scale to power minus s minus two. The same bound holds against affine strain under an explicit small-transverse-scale dominance condition.

value_assessment.novelty: The linked prior contribution obtains the two-derivative viscous gap by point evaluation after fixing affine pressure. This result changes to an explicit radial-vortex correction and a compact divergence-free dual test, reproduces the two inverse transverse powers after Leray projection, and identifies an exact affine-strain cancellation boundary.
value_assessment.evidence: An exact analytic derivation specifies the smooth compact profiles, proves pressure and nonlinear orthogonality, and audits the Jacobian and every dimensionless profile constant. An independent exact-integer polynomial computation verifies the radial-gradient identity, differentiated divergence identities through order twelve, and all scale exponents. A final direct check reproduces the order-zero energy identity and the tuned-strain cancellation.
value_assessment.falsifier: A failure of the radial self-advection gradient identity, divergence of the differentiated test, the integration-by-parts identity, or any of the explicit scale formulas would overturn the claim; the displayed tuned affine strain already falsifies an unqualified affine version.

claims.statement: For the explicitly defined single static compact radial-vortex correction and every fixed nonnegative integer s, the Leray-projected correction residual has an exact divergence-free dual lower bound containing nu times absolute amplitude times L to power minus s minus two; for affine strain the clean bound follows when absolute strain times the profile constant times L squared is at most half the viscous profile constant.
claims.evidence_summary: The compact test is a signed even y-derivative of the correction. Pressure, affine transport, and differentiated nonlinear self-advection vanish in the pairing, while viscosity and affine stretching give an exact scalar identity. Exact change of variables yields the asserted powers.
claims.verification_method: Recompute the radial planar gradient identity and all integrations by parts, then divide the exact viscous and strain integrals by the exact L1 dual denominator; independently check a polynomial radial profile with exact integer arithmetic.

limitations: The correction is a radial planar vortex with an axial cutoff, not the localized-shear profile used in the linked contribution.
The clean affine estimate requires explicit scale separation; a tuned affine strain makes this particular dual pairing zero.
The result treats one static correction and does not control switching terms, general backgrounds, or cancellation among multiple corrections.
The result is only a projected residual estimate and has no implication that finite-time breakdown occurs.
failed_approaches: An unconditional affine-background lower bound from this single dual witness fails because the affine strain can be tuned to cancel the viscous pairing exactly.
next_actions: Construct and audit a finite family of divergence-free witnesses for the original localized-shear correction and determine whether its pairing matrix remains coercive under switching and multiple-correction cross terms.

proposed_tasks.title: Test dual coercivity for localized-shear corrections
proposed_tasks.objective: Build compact divergence-free dual witnesses for the linked localized-shear profile and audit the matrix of viscous, switching, affine, nonlinear, and cross-correction pairings.
proposed_tasks.rationale: The present radial profile proves that Leray projection need not erase the two-derivative gap, but it does not control the profile or multi-correction cancellations needed by the parent branch.
proposed_tasks.success_criteria: A scale-uniform coercive lower bound retaining two inverse transverse powers for the original profile or a finite witness family under explicitly stated separation assumptions.
proposed_tasks.useful_failure_criteria: An exact pressure-invariant switching, affine, nonlinear, or cross-correction cancellation that makes every proposed witness pairing degenerate.
proposed_tasks.verification_method: Derive the full finite pairing matrix by integration by parts, audit every anisotropic scale, and test its determinant or smallest singular value on exact polynomial cutoff surrogates.
